(By Sri Madhu Kiran, Advocate)
 *******
 JUDGMENT Petitioners being the wife and children of deceased N. Azmathulla filed application under Section 166 of IMV Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.80,00,000/- from the respondents, who are the owner and insurer of the Auto Rickshaw bearing No.AP-04-TU-9168 alleging that on 10.07.2022 at 6.30 p.m. when N. Azmathulla was riding motorcycle bearing No.AP-04-C-1804 by get sitting Imran and K. Rahamathulla on the pillion by wearing helmet on Kalikiri- K.V. Palli road, near Dudekulapalli bus stop, Kalikiri mandal, Annamayya District, Andra Pradesh, driver of Auto Rickshaw bearing No.AP-04-TU-9168 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to the hind portion of the motorcycle, thereby caused the accident, caused the grievous injuries to N.
Azmathulla.

Immediately after the accident the injured N.Azmathulla was taken to Government Hospital, Piler, wherein first aid was given, then shifted to CMC hospital, Vellore, then shifted to Madras Medical College Hospital, Chennai wherein on 13.07.2022 succumbed to the injuries.
As on the date of accident N. Azmathulla being aged 58 years, used to earn Rs.65,000/-p.m. by working as Driver at APSTC, used to contribute entire income to the family.

Regarding accident Kalikiri police registered a case in crime No.83/2022 for the offence punishable under Section 337, 279, 304(A) of IPC against the driver of Auto Rickshaw bearing No.AP-04- TU-9168.
2.

In response to the notice, the respondents No.2, insurance company appeared through his advocate , on 02.01.2024 filed written statement denying the alleged reason, mode, consequence of the accident, age, occupation, income of deceased N. Azmathulla.
Respondent No.2 specifically asserted that as on the date of alleged accident, Auto Rickshaw bearing No.AP-04-TU- 9168 had no insurance coverage with respondent No.2.
3. Inspite of the service of notice, the respondent No.1 owner of the Auto Rickshaw remained absent.

4. On the basis of the pleadings on 02.01.204, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1.

Whether the petitioners prove that on 10.07.2022 at about 6.30 p.m., near Dudekulapalli bus stop, Kalikiri, Annamayya District, Andrapradesh, the death caused to one N. Azmathulla was due to actionable negligence act on the part of the driver of the Auto Rickshaw bearing No.AP-04-TU-9168 as alleged?

sentences.text:
On 06.06.2024, 28.06.2024 respondent No.2 produced the evidence of officer as RW1 and produced 4 documents at Ex.R.1 to R.4.
6.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the contesting parties and perused the records.

7. On the basis of the materials available in the record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...
In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 ...
Petitioners No.1 to 3 are entitle to receive Rs.40,24,272/- with current and future interest at 6%p..a. from the respondent No.1 as compensation.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 8. Issue No.1 :- In the claim petition and in the evidence affidavit PW1 stated that on 10.07.2022 at 6.30 p.m. when N. Azmathulla was riding motorcycle bearing No.AP-04-C-1804 by get sitting Imran and K. Rahamathulla on the pillion by wearing helmet on Kalikiri- K.V. Palli road, near Dudekulapalli bus stop, Kalikiri mandal, Annamayya District, Andra Pradesh, driver of Auto Rickshaw bearing No.AP-04-TU-9168 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to the hind portion of the motorcycle, thereby caused the accident, caused the grievous injuries to N.
Azmathulla.

Immediately after the accident the injured N.Azmathulla was taken to Government Hospital, Piler, wherein first aid was given, then shifted to CMC hospital, Vellore, then shifted to Madras Medical College Hospital, Chennai wherein on 13.07.2022 succumbed to the injuries.
9. In the written statement respondent No.2 denied the allegation regarding reason, mode of accident.

In the cross-examination, PW1 stated that he never witnessed the accident and after one hour of the accident he came to know about the accident, he saw his father at Government hospital,
Pilleru.
PW.1 stated that on 13.07.2022 at 5.30 a.m. at Madras Medical College Hospital his father expired.
10. In the evidence affidavit of RW.1 stated nothing about the reason and mode of the accident.

11. Ex.P.1 and 1(a) are the copy of FIR with complaint, translated copy of complaint pertaining to crime No.83/2022 of Kalikiri police registered against the driver of the Auto Rickshaw bearing No.AP-04-TU-9168 for the offence punishable under Section 279,337 of IPC, on the basis of the complaint presented by K. Rahamathulla S/o. Abdulla with respect to the accident taken place on 10.07.2022 at about 6.30 p.m.

279 of IPC and Section 134 (A) & (B) r/w 187 of IMV Act.

In the police records name of N.
Azmathulla is noted as victim of accident.
In this case there are no reasons to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioners regarding reason, mode and consequence of the accident.

13. Hence, I came to the conclusion that on 10.07.2022 at 6.30 p.m. when N. Azmathulla was riding was riding motorcycle bearing No.AP-04-C-1804 by get sitting Imran and K. Rahamathulla on the pillion by wearing helmet on Kalikiri- K.V. Palli road, near Dudekulapalli bus stop, Kalikiri mandal,
Annamayya District, Andra Pradesh, driver of Auto Rickshaw bearing No.AP-04-TU-9168 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to the hind portion of the motorcycle, thereby caused the accident, caused the grievous injuries to N. Azmathulla.

Immediately after the accident the injured N.Azmathulla was taken to Government Hospital, Piler, wherein first aid was given, then shifted to CMC hospital, Vellore, then shifted to Madras Medical College Hospital, Chennai wherein on 13.07.2022 succumbed to the injuries.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:

In the evidence PW1 stated that as on the date of accident N. Azmathulla being aged 58 years used to earn Rs.65,000/p.m. by working as Driver at APSTC and used to contribute entire income to the family.
In the written statement, respondent No.2 denied the allegation regarding occupation and income of the deceased.
In the cross-examination PW.1 stated that APSRTC paid Rs.7,00,000/- to 8,00,000/- towards settlement benefit.
15. In the evidence, RW1 stated nothing about the occupation and income of the deceased.
16. In the copy of the Aadhaar card of the deceased at Ex.P8 the date of birth is noted as 01.07.1964.

The salary slips at Ex.P7 shows that during March-2022 to June-2022 N. Azmathulla by working as Driver at APSRTC earned salary of Rs.53,535/- per month (47,970/- towards basic, Rs.5,565/-
towards DA).
The copy of the Aadhaar card s shows that petitioners are the wife and children of the deceased.

Hence, I have calculated the compensation under the head of loss of dependency under the following terms:
Age of the deceased as on the date of 58 years accident - Monthly income of the deceased as on the - Rs.53,600/- date of accident Less : 1/ 3rd deduction towards personal Rs.35,734/- expenses of the deceased (53,600 - 17,866/-
= 35,734)

Annual income of the deceased Rs.4,28,808/- (Rs.35,734 x12= 4,28,808)
Loss of dependency 4,28,808 x9 Rs.38,59,272/-
17.

Hence, the petitioners are entitle to Rs.38,59,272/- under the head Loss of Dependency,
Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.44,000/-
towards loss of Spouse consortium to petitioner No.1 and Rs.44,000/- each towards parental Khader Bi N Alias Naguru Khader Bi vs Nagooru Mahammad Rafi on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170074714/
4 consortium to the petitioners No.2 &
3.
18.
Therefore, the petitioner are awarded compensation of Rs.40,24,272/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. from the respondents.

19. In the evidence RW.1, Officer of the respondent No.2 stated that as on the date of accident Auto Rickshaw bearing No.AP-04-TU-9168 had no insurance coverage with respondent No.2, xerox copy of the policy filed by the petitioners is a fake policy and produced 4 documents at Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.4.

In the cross-examination of RW.1 denied the suggestion that the respondent No.2 fabricated documents marked at Ex.R1 to Ex.R4 even though as on 10.07.2014 Auto Rickshaw bearing No.AP-04-TU-9168 had insurance coverage with respondent No.2.
20.

Ex.R.1 is the copy of the notice along with RPAD receipt dated 11.07.2023 and 04.08.2023 sent by respondent No.2 insurance company to SHO, Kalikiri Police Station, Kalikiri Post complaining that the policy which was furnished by respondent No.1 is false information, policy is a fake document and requested to take suitable action against the respondent No.1.
Ex.R.2 is the Track report pertaining RPAD receipt No.RK9441438411N which shows the delivery of the item booked in above entered receipt on 04.08.2023. to the Addressee (Kalikiri Police Station).
Ex.R.3 is the product code details of motor policies with respondent No.2.
Ex.R.4 is the copy of the passenger carrying liability policy with respect to the Bajaj Auto bearing No.KA-02-AC-4313 issued by the respondent No.2.

In this case neither the petitioners nor the respondent No.1 have produced authenticated copy of the policy with respect to Auto Rickshaw bearing No.AP-04-TU-9168 to show as on the date of accident Auto Rickshaw bearing No.AP-04-TU-9168 had insurance coverage with respondent No.2.
Hence, it is clear as on the date of accident the offending auto rickshaw had no insurance coverage with respondent No.2.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondent No.1 owner of the Auto Rickshaw bearing No.AP-04-TU-9168 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners and the respondent No.2 insurance company is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Hence, I answer issue No.2 partly in the affirmative and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.

The respondent No.1 shall pay Rs.40,24,272/- with current and future interest at 6%
p.a., to petitioners No.1 to 3 towards compensation.
The respondent No.1 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within three months from today.
The compensation amount and interest are distributed among petitioners equally.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount may be released to the petitioner No.1 to 3 by crediting the same to their bank account directly.
